title: Authored gradients — the proportional scale of degrees between two opposed poles
note: The relational/proportional/associated triad's missing third. Where the weave gives an antonym couple as a binary AXIS (a clean cut) and a bit collapses an axis to its two poles (0/1, no between), a gradient FILLS the axis with degrees — proportion, meaning that is not yes/no but a position on a scale. `position` places each term in [0,1] from the low pole to the high; the midpoint (~0.50) is the BALANCE — the mean between the extremes, the very point a breath sign holds as a paradox (the labrys's opposed blades in balance; equilibrium). So the gradient and the paradox are one opposition seen two ways: the paradox holds both poles at the balance point; the gradient lays out the degrees between them. An authored proxy, surfaced here, not a measurement of where a word 'really' sits; descriptive, never a gate.

gradients.note: The plainest physical gradient — the paradigm of proportion: between cold and hot lie not one cut but a continuum of degrees.

Aristotle's doctrine of the mean — and equilibrium's own pump-era shard 'moderation': the balance between too little and too much. The midpoint of this gradient is the balance the labrys held whole as a paradox.
An experiential gradient: regard is not love-or-hate but a scale of degrees, with indifference the balance at its centre.
A perceptual gradient between dark and light, twilight the balance — perception reads degrees, not a switch.
